channel.title: Parallax
channel.description: Same event, different vantage points. Geopolitical news compared across Western, Eastern, Middle Eastern and Russian outlets.

item.title: Exit polls indicate Iliana Yotova has won the presidential runoff election in Bulgaria.
item.description: Iliana Yotova won the Bulgarian presidential runoff against Andrei Gyurov, with reports citing a victory margin between 52% and 57%. While both Western and Russian outlets confirm the result, they differ significantly in their framing of Yotova's platform. Western media emphasizes a domestic shift toward a "peace" narrative and dialogue with Moscow, whereas Russian reporting frames her victory as a strategic reaction to regional security tensions and a rejection of military aid to Ukraine.

item.title: United States push for resuming Russian gas sales to Europe via Ukraine faces Kremlin skepticism.
item.description: The United States is pushing for a "winter energy truce" to resume Russian natural gas flows to Europe through Ukrainian pipelines using a U.S. intermediary and an escrow payment system. Western outlets frame this as a proactive diplomatic push to stabilize European energy markets. Conversely, Russian reporting emphasizes the Kremlin's skepticism, framing the proposal as a remote possibility due to significant logistical and political hurdles. The coverage differs on whether the initiative represents an active negotiation or a remote possibility.

item.title: Fighting resumes in the Kherson region following the conclusion of a temporary ceasefire.
item.description: Fighting resumed in the Kherson region following a six-day ceasefire intended to evacuate civilians and deliver supplies to the town of Oleshky. While both Western and Russian sources agree on the timeline and humanitarian goals, they differ significantly in their framing of the truce's purpose. Western outlets focus on the diplomatic complexities and Ukrainian claims of Russian military repositioning, whereas Russian media emphasizes the successful completion of the humanitarian mission and the lack of violations.
